memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Nile will teem with frogs. They will come up into your palace and your bedroom and onto your bed, into the houses of your officials and on your people, and into your ovens and kneading troughs. The frogs will go up on you and your people and all your officials." - Exodus 8:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Read the list of places. The palace. The bedroom. The bed. The ovens. The kneading troughs. On you, and on your officials.

Nothing is out of reach. Pharaoh's throne room cannot keep them out, and neither can his bedroom door. In the last chapter he walked into his palace and shut the door on God's warning. Now the judgement follows him inside.

There is a sober truth here. We can close doors on people, but not on God. Nothing in our lives is hidden from Him — not our private rooms, not our screens, not our thoughts at night. Hebrews says everything is uncovered and laid bare before the eyes of Him to whom we must give account (Heb 4:13).

That is terrifying if we are hiding. It is enormous comfort if we are His. The God from whom nothing is hidden is the same God who knows our secret struggles, our unspoken grief, and the prayers we never manage to say aloud.

Bring Him into the rooms you keep shut.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which room of my life have I been trying to keep God out of?
2. Does God's total knowledge of me frighten me or comfort me — and why?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You see every part of my life. I open the doors I have kept closed. Come in and make me clean. Amen.
